title: CBDT extends Tax Audit deadline to October 21, ITR filing to November 21 for AY 2026-27
summary: CBDT extends the AY 2026-27 tax audit deadline to October 21 and ITR filing deadline to November 21, 2026. Check eligibility and revised dates.

# CBDT extends Tax Audit deadline to October 21, ITR filing to November 21 for AY 2026-27


Audit season just got a little breathing room. The[Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/cbdt) has pushed back two key dates for Assessment Year (AY) 2026-27. The tax audit report is now due on October 21, 2026, instead of September 30. The related ITR moves from October 31 to November 21, 2026. Before you start to celebrate, read this article. This isn't a free pass for everyone.


> The CBDT/Income Tax Department specifically refers to persons mentioned at Serial No. 2 in the table below Explanation 2 to Section 139(1), not taxpayers generally covered by Section 139(1). Consider stating that this includes companies and non-company assessees whose accounts are required to be audited, along with relevant partners of audited firms, where Section 92E does not apply. This will prevent readers from interpreting the November 21 deadline as applying to every taxpayer covered by Section 139(1).


## Revised Tax Audit and ITR deadlines


CBDT has changed two separate dates. They're linked, but they aren't the same thing.


Compliance Earlier deadline Revised deadline


Tax audit report September 30, 2026 October 21, 2026


ITR for specified audit cases October 31, 2026 November 21, 2026


The extension does not change the separate deadlines applicable to taxpayers covered by Section 92E (transfer-pricing cases). Their applicable return and reporting deadlines should be checked separately.


**Here is the link to the official**[Press Release](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2316050&lang=1&reg=3&utm) **issued by the government authorities.**


## Who gets the November 21 ITR deadline?


Only specified taxpayers whose accounts must be audited. CBDT points to Serial No. 2 in the table below Explanation 2 to Section 139(1) to mark out this group. So, the extension isn't a blanket change. Suppose you're a salaried employee who spotted a headline about November 21. That date doesn't automatically apply to you. Your deadline still depends on your own category and the rules that govern your return.


## What is the new Tax Audit deadline for AY 2026-27?


The tax audit report can now be furnished by October 21, 2026. The earlier cut-off was September 30. Certain businesses, professions and other specified cases need a tax audit under the Income-tax Act. If that's you, the audit must be completed and the report furnished within the deadline. The extra 21 days give you and your Chartered Accountant (CA) more room to reconcile figures and fix loose ends before the return goes in.


**Read more:**[‍Income Tax Audit: Deep dive into Section 44AB](https://getswipe.in/blog/article/income-tax-audit-section-44ab-guide) ****


## What is the new ITR filing deadline?


For covered taxpayers, the ITR deadline has shifted from October 31 to November 21, 2026. That's another 21 days. Here's why the two dates move together. A taxpayer may prepare substantial parts of the return before the audit is complete. A return can only be finalised once the financial data and audit details are settled. Think of it like building a house. You can't paint the walls until the plastering is done. The audit report comes first and the ITR follows.


### Does the extension apply to all taxpayers?


No. November 21 isn't a general ITR deadline for AY 2026-27. The announcement concerns taxpayers in the relevant audit category. Everyone else should follow the deadline that applies to their own filing category. This matters most for individuals who see the news and assume they can wait. Don't. Check your category first.


## Tax Audit report vs ITR: What's the difference?


The two documents do different jobs.


- A tax audit report carries prescribed details about your accounts and your financial and tax-related particulars. It's part of the audit compliance process.
- An Income Tax Return is how you report income, deductions and tax liability to the Income Tax Department.


For covered taxpayers, the order is simple. Furnish the audit report by October 21. Then file the ITR by November 21.


**Important:**[How to file Income Tax Return (ITR) online?](https://getswipe.in/blog/article/how-to-file-itr-income-tax-return-online) ****


## Why has CBDT extended the deadlines?


Audit work takes time. Someone has to review books of accounts, reconcile financial data, check tax records and prepare the prescribed reports. Only then can the ITR be finalized. Media reports also noted that tax professionals had asked for more time because of their workload. However, CBDT's official announcement mainly confirms the new dates and the covered category. It doesn't explain every reason behind the decision.


## What should taxpayers do now?


Use the extra time wisely. Don't treat it as an invitation to wait until the last day.


1. **Confirm your status.** Check whether your accounts need an audit and whether you fall in the covered category.
2. **Tidy your records.** Reconcile books, bank statements, invoices and expenses.
3. **Brief your CA early.** Share the required information so the audit report can be furnished by October 21, 2026.
4. **Prepare the ITR.** Once the audit details are final, file the applicable return by November 21, 2026.


Remember, these are two separate deadlines. They don't merge into one.


## AY 2026-27 Tax deadlines at a glance


Tax compliance Earlier deadline Revised deadline Applies to


Tax audit report September 30, 2026 October 21, 2026 Specified audit cases covered by the extension


ITR October 31, 2026 November 21, 2026 Specified audit cases covered by the extension


AY 2026-27 covers income earned in Financial Year (FY) 2025-26. Select the correct assessment year when you file.

## Conclusion


CBDT has extended the tax audit report deadline for specified taxpayers for AY 2026-27 from *September 30 to October 21, 2026*. The corresponding ITR filing deadline has also moved from *October 31 to November 21, 2026* for taxpayers covered by the specified category under Section 139(1).


The extension gives eligible businesses and professionals additional time to complete their audit, furnish the required report and file their ITR. However, taxpayers covered by *Section 92E, including applicable transfer-pricing cases, follow separate reporting and return-filing deadlines* and should not assume that the November 21 date applies to them.


Before relying on the revised dates, check your applicable filing category and the relevant provisions for AY 2026-27. If you are unsure which deadline applies, confirm it with your tax professional or refer to the latest CBDT notification.


## FAQs


### Does the November 21, 2026 deadline apply to transfer-pricing cases?


No. Taxpayers covered by Section 92E fall under a separate return-filing category. The applicable transfer-pricing reporting and ITR deadlines should be followed rather than assuming that the November 21 extension applies.


### What is the new tax audit deadline for AY 2026-27?


The audit report deadline for specified cases is now October 21, 2026. It was September 30.


### What is the new ITR filing deadline for audited taxpayers?


For covered taxpayers, the ITR deadline is now November 21, 2026. It was October 31.


### Who can file their ITR by November 21, 2026?


Taxpayers in the category CBDT specifies under Serial No. 2 in the table below Explanation 2 to Section 139(1) of the Income-tax Act, 1961.


### Does the CBDT extension apply to all taxpayers?


No. It applies only to taxpayers covered by the relevant audit provisions. Others must follow the deadline for their own category.


### What is the difference between the October 21 and November 21 deadlines?


October 21 is for furnishing the tax audit report. November 21 is for filing the corresponding ITR in specified audit cases.


### What should taxpayers do before October 21?


Finish your books and reconciliations. Hand the records to your CA. Complete the audit and make sure the report is furnished by the revised deadline.
